newsitem.title: UK: London gold sits pretty while silver sinks.
newsitem.headline: London gold sits pretty while silver sinks.

text.p: Silver prices sank further on Thursday afternoon after tumbling from rally highs overnight, while palladium fixed at a fresh three-year low.
"They're all just dribbling lower. The market is disappointed after another upside test was aborted," a dealer said of the white metals.
But gold shrugged off its stablemates' mounting losses, fixing barely changed at $380.60 an ounce, compared to $380.55 in the morning.
Gold also ignored news that Russian President Boris Yeltsin had sacked his security chief Alexander Lebed amid a Kremlin power struggle between Lebed and Russia's interior minister.
Gold had shed about $1.00 overnight after the silver-led rally failed, and New York's Comex December gold was down 60 cents at $384.60 an ounce.
Nevertheless, several dealers said gold was unlikely to move from its $380-$383 price range in the near term. It scurried higher after dipping briefly below the $380 support level.
Prices were being strangled by options, which give the right but not the obligation to buy or sell gold at a given price, several dealers said.

"Gold is absolutely rangebound and it seems there's little prospect of imminent collapse or a sustained climb," one said. "The thing to watch is what happens when the options expire at the end of the month." Silver, the current leader of the precious metals complex, was more volitile and reained vulnerable to revisiting recent lows around $4.80, dealers said.
Indicated at $4.92/$4.94 an ounce, silver had nosediving close to 15 cents since Wednesday's London close.
Palladium, under pressure from oversupply and slack demand, slid further to $115.00/$116.00, down $1.00.
It fixed at a fresh three-year low of $115.75 an ounce in the afternoon and flirted with levels as low as $114.75 an ounce.
Dealers said it had come under light selling pressure from investment funds in the afternoon.
Its sister metal platinum was also lower at $383.50/$384.50 an ounce, down $1.50 from the London close.
